concerns.text: T030 (Attribution), T031 (Alignment), and T032 (Clustering) are marked [P] (parallel-safe). However, T031 (Procrustes alignment) requires a 'common reference frame' derived from the set of high-importance substructures generated by T030. T032 (DBSCAN) requires the aligned output of T031. These tasks have a strict producer-consumer dependency (T030 -> T031 -> T032) and cannot run in parallel. The [P] tag is incorrect and violates the ordering lens.

T033 (t-tests), T034 (permutation), and T035 (FDR) are marked [P]. T035 (FDR correction) mathematically requires the p-values generated by T033 and T034 as input. T034 (permutation) often requires the baseline statistics from T033 or the same input data structure. These tasks form a sequential statistical pipeline (Generate Stats -> Permute -> Correct). Marking them as parallel-safe is a semantic ordering violation.

T016 (3D sensitivity analysis) is placed in Phase 3 (US1) but depends on the graph construction logic in T014. The task description says 'Re-run graph construction', implying it consumes the output of T014. However, T016 is marked [P] alongside T012-T015. If T016 runs in parallel with T014, it cannot access the 're-run' logic or the specific cutoff variations without a defined dependency or a separate execution context. The [P] tag is ambiguous and likely incorrect for a task that re-executes the core pipeline logic.

Phase 4 (Reporting) tasks T039-T042 are not explicitly marked with a [P] tag, but T042 (Generate final report) clearly depends on the aggregation results of T039, T040, and T041. The lack of explicit dependency notation or sequential ordering in the list (vs. the [P] tags in previous phases) creates ambiguity about whether T042 can start before T039-T041 complete. While likely sequential by nature, the ordering is not explicitly enforced by the task list structure.
